settings.title: AFFORDABLE Nil T2 Filing for Medicine Professional Corporations

settings.editor:
A professional corporation you are not billing through still files, especially while the certificate of authorization is held, the fiscal year end keeps running, and the entity stays on the college register. We file those years at $300.00 plus HST per tax year, for physicians who want the corporation current without a full engagement.

Whether you are on parental leave, away on a fellowship, moved to a salaried hospital appointment, or winding a locum practice down, we measure the year against billings and any investment income inside the corporation, prepare the return with Schedule 50 naming every shareholder at 10% or more, and transmit it electronically. A year the portfolio paid in goes to the full service.

settings.title: When a Medicine Professional Corporation Is Not Nil

settings.title_text: A Portfolio Sits Inside the Corporation
settings.description_text: Interest, dividends or a realised gain on investments the corporation owns is income to it, whoever manages them.
A year-end reconciliation from the provincial plan, or a shadow billing payment, counts in the year it arrives.
Salary or a dividend to a spouse or adult child holding non-voting shares is activity.
Goodwill, a patient list or examination equipment transferred to a buyer is a disposal.

settings.editor:
The portfolio is what catches physicians out. Retained earnings left inside a professional corporation are very often invested, and the moment those holdings pay interest or a dividend the corporation has income, even in a year its physician saw no patients through it. Passive investment income also carries treatment of its own, which a nil return does not provide.

Such a year is an ordinary corporate return. Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation takes it at gondaliyacpa.ca, where the fee is $350.00 plus HST per year. Only a year in which the corporation neither earned nor paid anything belongs on this page, at $300.00 plus HST per tax year.

settings.title_text: Investment Income Ends a Nil Year
settings.description_text: One dividend or interest credit inside the corporation puts a figure on Schedule 125 and makes the year an ordinary return.
A certificate of authorization renews on the college cycle. The T2 does not renew it and the college does not file it.
A balance carried forward from practising years sits on Schedule 100 without making the year active, provided it earned nothing.

settings.html:
The year is nil

  • Nothing was billed to the provincial plan through the corporation
  • No private, insurance or third-party fee was invoiced by it
  • No investment it owns paid interest, a dividend or a gain
  • No salary or dividend went to any shareholder
  • No equipment, goodwill or patient list was sold or transferred

The year is not nil

  • A reconciliation or shadow billing payment arrived from the plan
  • A portfolio inside the corporation paid interest, dividends or a gain
  • A spouse or adult child shareholder drew salary or a dividend
  • The practice, its goodwill or its patient list was sold
  • The corporation paid rent, staff or an association fee

Due either way

  • A T2 for every tax year the corporation exists
  • A T183CORP signed by an authorised signing officer, per tax year
  • Schedule 50, naming every shareholder at 10% or more
  • The certificate of authorization, renewed with the college separately
  • A record of what was billed, which decides the year either way

settings.title: Nil T2 Filing Cost for a Medicine Professional Corporation

settings.editor: Nil T2 filing is $300.00 plus HST per tax year. The fee covers the T2, the GIFI schedules where required, Schedule 50, Schedule 24 on a first return, the T183CORP package with secure e-signing, CPA review before transmission, electronic transmission by a registered EFILE electronic filer, one corrected transmission where the Agency rejects the first, and the CRA confirmation emailed within 3 business days. A year with billings or investment income inside the corporation is $350.00 plus HST per year at gondaliyacpa.ca.

Medicine professional corporations are filed the same way wherever the registered office sits, because the return is prepared and transmitted electronically from end to end. There is nothing to print, nothing to post and nothing to sign in person.

Where the corporation was incorporated changes the registry, not the return. An Ontario corporation answers to the Ontario Business Registry, and corporations in British Columbia, Alberta, Quebec and Saskatchewan each answer to their own. The T2 itself is federal and identical in all of them. Within Ontario, a corporation registered in Toronto, Mississauga, Brampton or Ottawa is filed on the same terms and at the same price as one anywhere else in the country.

Two provinces add a return the federal T2 does not cover. A Quebec corporation also files the CO-17 and an Alberta corporation also files the AT1. Both are separate provincial returns, and neither is included in the $300.00 plus HST fee.
